subject: Skyline Health: peak-window p95 carveout request and internal asks

Subject: Request: p95 target during peak windows

Hi Vivek —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We've started a small pilot and are seeing very promising accuracy, but our ops team flagged latency spikes during our morning and evening peaks (roughly 08:00–10:00 PST and 18:00–20:00 PST). Attached is a short sample trace and percentile breakdown from our integration tests.

Ask: would Redwood consider a targeted p95 commitment for those two daily windows for the initial 6-week pilot? Our internal target is p95 < 100ms end-to-end for the request pattern in the attached. We understand this is an exception and are open to compensating terms (capacity reservation, higher commit, credits for misses).

If feasible, can you loop in product/infra/legal so we can fast-track a short-term amendment to our trial agreement? We're aiming to take to procurement by July 20.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

Elena — appreciate the data and clear ask. Looping in product (Karthik), infra/ops (Grace) and legal (Laura) to confirm feasibility and the minimal set of controls we would need to make a short-term carveout.

High level from sales: Skyline is a strategic pilot for us in the digital health space. They're asking for p95 < 100ms for two daily 2-hour windows for a 6-week pilot. They are willing to take reserved capacity or higher commit to get this. Procurement timeline: July 20.

Karthik/Grace/Laura — can you help with: 1) technical feasibility and whether we can offer a time-bound carveout for those windows, 2) what operational guarantees/runbook we require, and 3) suggested contract language or risk mitigations (credits, caps, fallbacks) so legal can draft an amendment quickly?

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-12T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: p95 target during peak windows

Thanks for the ping — quick read of the attachment looks like the request is concentrated on short inference flows (few tokens) but high throughput during the windows. From product POV a conditional carveout could work if we pair it with operational constraints and fallbacks. Proposed terms to evaluate: 

- Scope: time-bound (6 weeks) pilot carveout limited to two daily windows (08:00–10:00 PST, 18:00–20:00 PST) and a single model revision pinned for the duration.
- Capacity: require reserved burst pool (dedicated queue) with XYZ qps guarantee for the windows; customer pays a temporary reserved capacity premium.
- Traffic shaping & routing: forward requests for that route to dedicated pool; traffic overage will fall back to baseline model variant (grace's team should configure automatic fallback).
- Warm-up & cache: require a 30-minute warm-up plan before each window (pre-warming prefixes, KV cache priming).
- Observability & alerts: per-route latency SLO dashboard + real-time paging to both RW oncall and Skyline on-call.
- Credits & SLA: define miss credit formula (e.g., credits for minutes of p95 > threshold) and a cap on exposure (monthly cap or dollar cap).

Open questions for infra/ops: what's the realistic QPS we can guarantee for a dedicated pool in our current Dedicated offering? Grace — do we have a safe default for overage fallback latency and what ops runbook changes would be required?

Laura — from legal: we'll need a short amendment that limits our exposure and mandates the warm-up/observability steps above. If they accept reserved capacity + capped credit exposure, we should be able to move fast.

Happy to join a call with Skyline to walk these tradeoffs.

— Karthik
Director, Product Management, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-13T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: p95 target during peak windows

Quick operational take — feasible with guardrails. Draft runbook summary (attached as operational-runbook-draft.md):

1) Dedicated pool sizing: we can provision a 5-node A100 equivalent pool for the windows (est. sustained 450 qps for the short flows Elena shared). Lead time: 48 hours after signed reserve.
2) Warm-up plan: 30-min automated prefix replay + KV cache seeding job; ops will run a validation load (script attached in runbook) 15m before go-live each window.
3) Fallback behavior: if observed cluster CPU/GPU or queue wait > threshold, auto-route overflow to baseline fleet (expected p95 ~ 220–300ms depending on load).
4) Monitoring: per-route telemetry with 10s granularity; we will create a dedicated dashboard and a webhook to Skyline's Ops slack/alert endpoint.
5) Incident playbook: on-call escalation to Redwood infra -> triage -> if rollout required we have a pre-approved fast rollback to baseline.

Risk & mitigations: cold-starts are the biggest risk — cache warming is mandatory in contract. We also recommend limiting allowed model changes (pin the served model version).

Attachments: operational-runbook-draft.md (includes sizing calc and validation script)

— Grace
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Elena — thanks for the patience and for the data. Quick summary and next steps so we can align with procurement: 

- Feasible path: Redwood can offer a 6-week, time-bound carveout limited to the two daily peak windows (08:00–10:00 PST, 18:00–20:00 PST) provided Skyline agrees to: reserved capacity (5-node equivalent) for those windows, mandatory 30-minute warm-up before each window, pinned model version, and an agreed credit formula with a cap.

- Expected fallbacks: if the dedicated pool exceeds thresholds we'll auto-route overflow to baseline fleet (expected p95 in fallback ~220–300ms).

- Legal & commercial: Laura will draft a short amendment that includes the warm-up requirement, committed reserved capacity fees, the credit formula, and an explicit exposure cap. Karthik and Grace will deliver the final runbook and sizing calc.

Action items and timeline:
1) Laura to send amendment draft by EOD Wed (2025-07-16).
2) Skyline accepts reserved capacity terms + countersign by July 18 to allow provisioning (48h lead time).
3) We schedule a 30m technical alignment call (Grace + Karthik + Skyline Ops) on July 18 or 19 — please indicate preferred times.
